drills.q: Compute LTV: $29 ARPU, 68% gross margin, 4%/mo churn.
drills.a: Lifetime = 1/0.04 = 25 months; LTV = 29 x 0.68 x 25 ~= $493. With CAC of $150 that's LTV:CAC ~= 3.3x (passes the >=3 heuristic) and payback = 150/(29x0.68) ~= 7.6 months.

drills.q: Cost per request: 800 input + 400 output tokens, $0.25/Mtok in, $1/Mtok out (small model).
drills.a: 800/1e6 x $0.25 = $0.0002; 400/1e6 x $1 = $0.0004; total $0.0006/request - ~21x cheaper than the frontier example ($0.0126). This ratio is what makes cascades transformative.

drills.q: Why is comparing paid-channel CAC against blended LTV self-deception?
drills.a: Blended LTV includes organic/referred users who cost little to acquire and often retain better; pairing it with paid CAC makes paid channels look far healthier than they are. Compare paid CAC against paid-cohort LTV, or compare both on a blended basis - consistently.

drills.q: Build the unit economics: AI feature, $29 seat, 25% free users, median 8 req/wk x2 skew, $0.0126/req, plus $2.10 support+hosting/user/mo.
drills.a: Token COGS mean = 8 x 4.33 x 0.0126 x 2 ~= $0.87; total COGS ~$2.97/user/mo. Blended ARPU = 29 x 0.75 = $21.75. Gross profit ~$18.8 -> GM ~86% blended... but recompute free-rider share of COGS carefully: if free users consume equally, paying users carry their COGS too - sensitivity table mandatory.

drills.q: Design usage-based pricing protecting margin for an AI tutoring assistant.
drills.a: Seat priced off median-user COGS at target GM covering ~P80 usage; metered credits beyond allowance at 3-5x marginal COGS (support/variance/free-rider subsidy); hard caps or degressive pricing on agent-style loops; cheap pricing for cached/batch paths to shape demand. Model the distribution, not the average.

drills.q: Business case for 2 quarters cutting inference cost 40%: walk it and say when you'd reject your own project.
drills.a: Current annualized COGS x 40% = recurring savings vs eng cost $400-800K; express payback months + 3yr NPV; add strategic kicker (enables free tier/pricing moves). If current spend is only ~$300K/yr, reject: propose caching config instead. Showing when NOT to do your own project is credibility gold.

drills.q: Your eval sweep shows mid-tier model within 3pts of frontier at 8x lower cost, but 2% of cases fail badly. Architecture?
drills.a: Cascade with confidence routing: mid-tier answers most traffic; uncertain/low-confidence cases escalate to frontier. You buy frontier quality exactly where failures concentrate while paying commodity prices elsewhere - typically recovers most of the gap at a fraction of full-frontier cost.

drills.q: Cohort analysis reveals new-channel acquisitions retain half as long. Actions?
drills.a: Recompute cohort/channel-level LTV and payback; pause channels whose cohort-LTV < CAC despite okay blends; adjust targeting toward retained-profile lookalikes; write falsifiable 'retention improves with maturity' bets with mechanisms and checkpoints if leadership wants to continue - hope isn't a mechanism.

drills.q: An agent product burns 50x single-shot tokens per task. Options?
drills.a: (1) Price like labor - reposition competitor set from software to people; (2) engineer token intensity: aggressive context management, small-model substeps, caching of tool outputs; (3) restrict agent loops with budgets/caps; (4) charge per outcome/task not per seat so COGS scales with willingness-to-pay. Unmanaged, 50x burn destroys any seat-price model.

drills.q: Finance challenges your engagement-uplift value claim. What do you bring?
drills.a: The full chain with confidence labels ($4-8M/yr band from module-01 method) PLUS the incremental serving bill from measured compute deltas, netted into margin impact, with a sensitivity table (engagement halved, compute doubled still clears zero). Volunteering both sides preempts silent re-derivation and buys credibility for future claims.
